The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this chapter, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning.
Abandoned animal means an animal that is owned or stray, unattended, and uncared for and additionally:
(1) Has been placed or is found on public property or within a public building; or
(2) Has been placed or is found on private property or within a private building without the consent of the private property owner, custodian, or tenant; or
(3) Is on or within the property of the animal's owner or custodian and has remained unattended or uncared for in excess of 36 hours.
Adequate food and water means wholesome food and water that is sufficient in quality and quantity and consisting of essential materials for good health, growth, and general life functions, and is appropriate for the particular type of animal consistent with the normal requirements and feeding habits of the animal's size, age, species, breed, and physical condition. This shall also include clean water in sufficient quantity and quality to sustain vital functions of the animal and provide sufficient hydration consistent with the normal requirements and drinking habits of the animal's size, age, species, and breed, and to which the animal has constant access. Both food and water must be in containers designed and situated to allow the animal easy access to them. The term "adequate food and water" also means food and water that is sufficient in quality, quantity, and accessibility so as to prevent starvation, dehydration, or a significant risk to the animal's health from a lack of proper quantity and quality of food or water.
Adequate shelter means a pen, structure, lean-to, animal house, or other provision to provide shelter to the animal from the extreme cold, heat, sun, or other climatic elements, and designed to keep the animal off the ground. It must be of sufficient size, design, and dimensions to allow the animal reasonable ability to stand up and turn around, to permit sufficient ventilation, and which is otherwise adequate given the animal's size, age, species, breed, and physical condition. Such shelter must at a minimum have three sides, a roof, and a floor.
Animal means any live creature, both domestic and wild, except humans. The term "animal" also includes birds, fish, and reptiles.
Animal enforcement agent means an employee of the animal control unit and any other law enforcement officers or other official of the city or county authorized by the city council to enforce the provisions of this chapter.
Animal nuisance means any nuisance arising out of the keeping, maintaining, owning of, or failure to exercise sufficient control over, an animal.
At heel means that a dog is directly behind or next to a person and obedient to that person's command under all circumstances.
At large means that an animal is off the premises of its owner or custodian and not on a leash or otherwise under the immediate control of a person physically capable of restraining the animal. With regard to dogs and cats, "at large" means any public nuisance dog or cat or any dog or cat causing a disturbance while not on a leash or in the vicinity of the owner and obedient to that person's commands. A dog or cat is not running at large when he is confined within the limits of his owner's property.
Cat means any member of the animal species felis catus or felis domesticus.
Certificate of registration means a current valid certificate of registration for the possession of a dangerous dog or a potentially dangerous dog issued pursuant to this chapter.
Cruelty means any act of commission or omission whereby unjustifiable physical or mental pain or suffering, abuse, overwork, maiming, disfigurement, or death of an animal is caused or permitted, including, without limitation, failure to provide nutritious and adequate food, clean and adequate water, clean and adequate air for breathing, proper and adequate ventilation, proper and adequate space, shelter, and protection from the elements, a sanitary and safe living environment, or necessary veterinary care. In the case of bona fide activities where physical pain is necessarily caused, such as medical and scientific research, food processing, customary and normal veterinary and agricultural husbandry practices, pest elimination, and animal training and hunting, the term "cruelty" shall mean a failure to employ the most humane method reasonably available.
Dangerous dog means any dog that, according to records of an appropriate authority, inflicts severe injury on human beings without provocation on public or private property or aggressively bites, attacks, or endangers the safety of human beings without provocation after the dog has been classified as a potentially dangerous dog and after the owner has been notified of such classification.
Disposition means adoption, quarantine, voluntary or involuntary custodianship or placement, or euthanasia humanely administered to an animal in accordance with O.C.G.A. § 4-11-5.1. The term "disposition" also includes placement or sale of an animal to the general public.
Dog means any member of the animal species canis familiaris.
Guard or attack dog means a dog trained to attack on command or to protect persons or property, and who will cease to attack upon command.
Hopelessly disabled animal means any animal which is the subject of any disease, injury, or condition which is a cause of immediate and significant suffering by the animal and from which there is no reasonable probability of recovery.
Humane care means, but is not limited to, the provision of adequate heat, ventilation, sanitary shelter, and wholesome and adequate food and water, in each case consistent with the normal requirements and feeding habits of the animal's size, age, species, breed, and physical condition.
Hunting dog means any dog that is a member of a breed of dog recognized by the state department of natural resources as a hunting dog and is actively used by its owner for hunting purposes.
Hunting season means the seasons of the year designated and recognized by the state department of natural resources as being a hunting season.
Impound or impoundment means the taking into custody of an animal by any law enforcement official, or any authorized representative thereof.
Law enforcement officer means any law enforcement officer empowered to make arrest in this city.
Owner means any natural person or any legal entity, including, but not limited to, a corporation, partnership, firm or trust owning, possessing, harboring, keeping or having custody or control of a dog or cat within the incorporated area of the city.
Potentially dangerous dog means any dog that, without provocation, bites a human being on public or private property or acts in a threatening or aggressive manner towards a person that places said person in reasonable apprehension of immediately receiving a violent injury.
Proper enclosure and proper secure enclosure means an enclosure for keeping a dangerous dog or potentially dangerous dog, while on the owner's property, securely confined indoors or in a securely enclosed and locked pen, fence, or structure suitable to prevent the entry of young children and designed to prevent the dog from escaping. Any such pen or structure shall have secure sides and a secure top, and if the dog is enclosed within a fence, all sides of the fence shall be of sufficient height and the bottom of the fence shall be constructed or secured in such a manner as to prevent the dog's escape either from, over, through, or from under the fence. Any such enclosure shall also provide protection from the elements and sufficient ventilation for the dog.
Public nuisance animal means any animal that unreasonably annoys humans, endangers the life or health of persons or other animals, or substantially interferes with the rights of citizens, other than their owners, to enjoyment of life or property. The term "public nuisance animal" shall include but not be limited to:
(1) Any animal that is repeatedly found running or roaming at large.
(2) Any dog or cat in any section of a park or public recreation area, unless the dog or cat is under restraint by way of a leash or similar physical restraint; however, this provision shall not apply to any park or recreation facility specifically designed or provided for the purpose of a dog or animal park, whether such designation is temporary or permanent. Public nuisance dogs and cats include dogs and cats that have damaged property of anyone other than the owner thereof in the amount of $10.00 or more or any dog or cat causing unsanitary conditions in any enclosure or surroundings.
(3) Any animal that repeatedly damages or destroys any property other than that of its owner.
(4) Any animal that repeatedly soils, defiles, or defecates on any property other than that of its owner.
(5) Any animal that repeatedly makes disturbing noises, including, but not limited to, continued and repeated howling, barking, whining, or other utterances causing unreasonable annoyance, disturbance, or discomfort to neighbors or others in close proximity to the premises where the animal is kept or harbored.
(6) Any animal that causes or is left in unsanitary or unhealthy conditions created by an accumulation of excreta, or that causes fouling of the air by noxious or offensive odors due to unsanitary or unhealthy conditions and thereby creates unreasonable annoyance or discomfort to neighbors or others in close proximity to the premises where the animal is kept or harbored.
(7) Any animal in heat that is not confined so as to prevent attraction or contact with other animals of the same species or breed.
(8) Any animal, whether or not on the property of its owner, that:
a. Without provocation, molests, attacks, threatens, or otherwise interferes with the freedom of movement of persons in a public right-of-way;
b. Creates a traffic obstruction by their presence in the public right-of-way for vehicular traffic, bicyclists, or pedestrians.
(9) Any animal that, without provocation, attacks or threatens domestic animals.
(10) Any animal that is a danger to the public health, safety, or welfare by virtue of the number of animals maintained at a single location or the inadequacy of the facilities for such animals.
Rabies control tag means a valid tag evidencing the currently in effect annual inoculation against rabies of a dog, cat, or ferret, as the case may be, by a licensed veterinarian or other rabies inoculator approved under state law, rules and regulations.
Responsible person means a competent person of at least 18 years of age.
Sanitary means a condition of good order and cleanliness to minimize the possibility of disease creation or transmission and of unhealthy conditions.
Severe injury means any physical injury that results in broken bones or disfiguring lacerations requiring multiple sutures or cosmetic surgery or a physical injury that results in death.
Sexually mature animal means any dog or cat that has reached the age of six months or more or an animal that has come into heat-estrous or has the ability to breed and create a pregnancy.
Sterilization means the surgical removal of the reproductive organs of a dog or cat in order to render the animal unable to reproduce. Similarly, the term "sterilized" means when a dog or cat has undergone sterilization.
Stray cat means any cat which is found off the property of its owner, is not under restraint, and without attached to such cat a valid rabies control tag together with an identification microchip, tattoo, or tag.
Stray dog means any dog which is found off the property of its owner, is not under restraint, and without attached to such dog a valid rabies control tag together with an identification microchip, tattoo, or tag.
Under restraint means that an animal is secured by a leash, lead, or chain of sufficient tensile strength held by a person of sufficient age who is physically capable of restraining the animal and obedient to that person's commands, is at heel, or is securely enclosed within the real property limits of the owner's property.
Unsanitary conditions means any condition that is not sanitary, including, but not limited to, a buildup of excreta, spoiled or moldy food, unclean or stagnant water, pests, vermin, and any health code violation.
Vicious animal means any animal that attacks, bites or injures pets, companion animals or livestock or which, because of temperament, conditioning, or training, has a known propensity to attack, bite, or injure pets, companion animals, or livestock. No animal my be declared vicious if a threat, injury or damage was sustained by a pet, companion animal or livestock that, at the time, was committing a willful trespass or other tort upon the premises occupied by the owner or keeper of the animal. The term "vicious animal" shall not be construed to include dogs that are part of a governmental organization in the performance of its duties.
Vicious dog means a dog that, without provocation, has bitten or attempted to bite any person or another animal.
Without provocation and unprovoked mean that the animal at issue was not or had not been assaulted, teased, tormented, or abused by the person or domestic animal which was the subject of the act by the animal at issue, or that the animal at issue was not coming to the aid of or defending its young or was not acting against a person who was willfully trespassing or committing another willful tort or criminal act on the premises of such animal at issue's owner or custodian.
(Ord. of 3-11-2002, §§ 9-3-11, 9-3-24; Ord. of 9-8-2008, § II(9-2-4(B)))

(b) It shall be the duty of the chief of police to impound any and all cattle, cows, calves, horses or other domestic fowl or livestock found at large within the corporate limits of the city, and advertise same by posting a full description of such cattle, hogs, horses or other domestic fowl or livestock and giving the date and place where they shall be sold.
(c) After such animal or animals have been advertised for sale five days as indicated above, it shall be the duty of the chief of police to sell such animal or animals, and to deduct from the proceeds of the sale a fee in the amount provided in the city fee schedule for impoundment, advertising, daily board and feed.
(d) The owner may redeem the animal by paying the chief of police the fees and expenses specified in this section.
(Code 1989, § 9-3-2(a))
State Law reference— Livestock running at large, O.C.G.A. § 4-3-1 et seq.; disposal of impounded livestock, O.C.G.A. § 4-3-7.
239:
It is unlawful to keep any live swine or pigs within the city limits.
(Code 1989, § 9-3-3)
240:
Any housing or enclosure used for the keeping of animals or fowl shall be well drained, free from accumulations of animal excrement and objectionable odors, and otherwise clean and sanitary.
(Code 1989, § 9-3-4)
241:
It is unlawful for any person to inflict, cause or permit cruelty to or upon any animal, including without limitation to negligently, willfully or maliciously strike, beat, physically, or mentally abuse, overwork, overload, maim or disfigure, intentionally chase or run down with a vehicle, bicycle, or motorized or powered implement, or otherwise engage in any act or omission causing, inflicting, or resulting in unnecessary pain, injury, physical or mental suffering, abuse, or death to an animal, in each case taking into account the animal's age, size, physical condition, breed, and species, except that reasonable force may be used in self-defense to destroy a vicious or dangerous animals or to drive away trespassing animals as authorized by state law. Examples of acts prohibited by this section include, but are not limited to:
(1) Allowing a collar, rope, chain, or other item to become embedded in or cause injury to an animal's neck or other portion of the body.
(2) Allowing a slip type choke, or pinch type collar to be used as a primary collar to tether an animal.
(3) Intentionally causing or allowing animals to engage in a fight.
(4) Allowing animals to live in unsanitary conditions.
(5) Allowing animals to live in regularly over-crowded conditions.
(6) Failure or refusal to obtain veterinary medical treatment for an animal when, in the opinion of a veterinarian, a law enforcement official, or any officer authorized to enforce the provisions of this chapter, such treatment is needed.
(7) Shooting a domestic animal, either on or off of the owner's property, unless such domestic animal is then in the act of attacking or maliciously chasing a human being, horse, hog, goat, poultry, any other domestic animal or sheep or cattle, and shooting such domestic animal is then the most reasonable action under the particular circumstance, except under the direction of a veterinarian or law enforcement official where the animal is hopelessly suffering.
(Code 1989, § 9-3-5; Ord. of 9-8-2008, § II(9-2-4(K)(a))
State Law reference— Animal protection, O.C.G.A. § 4-11-1 et seq.; performing cruel acts on, harming, maiming or killing dogs, O.C.G.A. § 4-8-1.
242:
It shall be unlawful for any person to intentionally administer poison to any animal, or knowingly leave any poisonous substance of any kind or ground glass or other harmful substance in any place with the intent to injure any animal. This provision is not applicable to licensed pest control exterminators using poisons as part of an insect pest control program or the use of commercial insecticides, rodenticides, or rodent baits used to control insect and wild rodents, or to licensed veterinarians using veterinary pharmaceuticals in providing bona fide veterinary services.
(Ord. of 9-8-2008, § II(9-2-4(K)(b))
243: The animal control department may use any force reasonably necessary to remove any animal locked in a closed vehicle if the owner cannot be immediately located. The operator of the vehicle will be charged with cruelty to animals as defined in this chapter. No injunction or claim for damages may be placed against the animal control department or its officers for this action.
244:
(a) No person owning any dog or any other animal shall suffer or permit such animal to disturb the peace and quiet of the neighborhood by barking, making other loud or unusual noises, or by running through or across cultivated gardens, lawns, or fields.
(b) No owner or custodian of any animal shall fail to exercise proper care and control of such animal to prevent the same from becoming a public nuisance. It shall be unlawful for any person to keep any animal on any property located within the city when the keeping of such animal constitutes a public nuisance or menace to public health, welfare, or safety.
(Code 1989, § 9-3-6; Ord. of 9-8-2008, § II(9-2-4(D)(3), (H))
245:
It shall be the duty of the owner or person in custody of any animal kept in the city to have the animal inoculated against rabies at least once each year. The certification along with owner identification must be worn around the animal's neck at all times. The owner of an animal subject to this section must possess a current certification of rabies vaccination for each animal owned as provided for by state law.
(Ord. of 3-11-2002, §§ 9-3-8, 9-3-15)
State Law reference— Responsibility for control of rabies, O.C.G.A. § 31-19-1.
246:
The entire area embraced within the corporate limits of the city is designated as a bird sanctuary. It is unlawful to trap, hunt, molest or kill any wild bird or to rob any wild bird's nest; provided, however, if nuisance birds such as starlings are found to be congregating in such numbers in a particular locality so as to constitute a nuisance or a menace to health or property in the opinion of the city council, those birds may be destroyed as humanely as possible, under the supervision of the police department, in such numbers and in such manner as is deemed advisable by the city council.
(Code 1989, § 9-3-1)
247:
It is unlawful to trap, hunt, disturb or kill any other wild game in the city except by order of the chief of police.
(Code 1989, § 9-3-1)
248:
Licensed veterinarians, federal, state, and local law enforcement officials, and those authorized by the city manager to administer and enforce the provisions of this section, in each case while acting within the scope of their authority, are authorized to induce the death of hopelessly disabled animals by an appropriately humane method.
(Ord. of 9-8-2008, § II(9-2-4(C)(1))
249:
(a) In any situation deemed appropriate by an animal services officer involving a sick, diseased, or infected animal which sickness or disease, in the opinion of a licensed veterinarian, or a state or federal employee acting within the scope of his authority, will likely spread to other animals or humans, an authorized officer may impound and take custody of any such animal, the animal shall be isolated, and the owner or custodian of such animal shall be promptly notified.
(b) If the owner or custodian cannot be located, the owner or custodian fails to take immediate steps to remove the animal from impoundment, and take immediate steps to isolate the animal to properly eliminate the likelihood of infecting other animals or humans or otherwise spreading the sickness, disease, or infection, or, if in the opinion of a licensed veterinarian, destroying the animal is the most reasonable course of action to eliminate the health or safety risk of the animal spreading the sickness, disease, or infection, then in any such event, the infected animal shall be humanely destroyed in accordance with state law.
(c) The owner of any such animal impounded pursuant to this section shall be liable for reimbursement to the city or county, or both, as appropriate for all expenses related to the impoundment, boarding, treatment, and destruction of any such animal.
(Ord. of 9-8-2008, § II(9-2-4(C)(2))
252:
(a) It shall be the duty of every owner or custodian of any vicious animal to ensure that it is kept under restraint and that reasonable care and precautions are taken to prevent it from leaving the real property limits of its owner, possessor, or custodian, and ensure compliance with the provisions of this division.
(b) It shall be unlawful for an owner or custodian of a vicious dog to permit the dog within the city to be outside a proper, secure enclosure unless the dog is restrained by a substantial chain or leash and is under the physical restraint of a responsible person.
(Ord. of 3-11-2002, § 9-3-34; Ord. of 9-8-2008, § II(9-2-4(C))
253:
(a) Compliance required. It is unlawful for any person to cause, permit, accompany or be responsible for the presence of any vicious dog or cat on the streets or public places of the city or allow the animal to run on the premises of another, at any time except in compliance with this section.
(b) Enclosure. Every vicious or dangerous animal shall be securely and humanely enclosed within a house, building, fence, pen or other enclosure out of which it cannot climb, dig, jump, or otherwise escape on its own volition. Such enclosure is securely locked at any time the animal is left unattended.
(c) Leashing. Whenever the animal is outside of its enclosure as provided for above, but on the owner's property, it must be attended by the owner and restrained by a secure collar and leash of sufficient strength to prevent escape. The leash shall be no longer than ten feet, and the animal must be kept at least 15 feet within the perimeter boundaries of the property unless the perimeter is securely fenced.
(d) Tethering. No vicious animal shall be chained, tethered, or otherwise tied to any inanimate object such as a tree, post, or building, outside of an enclosure meeting the specifications of this section.
(e) Muzzling. If any persons shall cause, permit, accompany or be responsible for the presence of any vicious dog or cat on the streets or in public places within the city or on the premises of another, the animal shall be securely muzzled to effectively prevent it from biting any person or another animal.
(Ord. of 3-11-2002, § 9-3-34(1)—(4))
254:
All enclosures or housing units for vicious and dangerous animals will be inspected by the animal control agent.
(Ord. of 3-11-2002, § 9-3-34(5))
255:
(a) Impoundment. An animal may be immediately confiscated and held by any law enforcement official, or those authorized by the city to administer and enforce the provisions of this chapter, while acting within the scope of their respective authority, if the animal without provocation has:
(1) Killed, bitten, or otherwise severely injured a person or another domestic animal;
(2) Repeatedly chased or otherwise threatened persons or other domestic animals in a vicious or menacing manner indicating a reasonable likelihood that the animal will cause imminent physical injury; or
(3) Repeatedly caused significant damage to the property of other than that of its owner or custodian.
The impounded animal shall be confined in the county animal shelter pending a hearing, if necessary, to determine whether such animal should be destroyed as a public nuisance and, if not, in the case of a dog, classified as a dangerous dog or potentially dangerous dog.
(b) Notice to owner. The owner of any animal that has been so confiscated shall be given notice of said animal's confiscation. The notice to the owner shall be in writing and sent by certified mail or statutory overnight delivery to the last known address of the owner. The notice shall give a description of the animal and set forth the reasons that the animal has been confiscated, together with the date, time, and place of the hearing.
(c) Time for holding hearing. A hearing before the city shall be scheduled within 15 days from the date of notice to the owner of the animal's confiscation to determine if the animal should be destroyed as a public nuisance. At said hearing, the owner of the confiscated animal shall have the right to present testimony and evidence as to why the animal should not be destroyed as a public nuisance.
(d) Factors to be considered at hearing. The city, after receiving all pertinent testimony and evidence on the matter, shall decide whether the animal shall be destroyed as a public nuisance. In making its decision, the city shall consider whether the animal constitutes such a physical threat to persons or other animals, or of significant destruction or harm to property, by virtue of one or more unprovoked attacks on persons, other domestic animals, or physical property that destruction of the animal is reasonably necessary to protect the health, welfare, or property in the city.
(e) Determination that animal must be destroyed. If the city decides that said animal should be destroyed, then the owner shall promptly be given written notice thereof, and the animal shall be humanely destroyed any time after five business days after the date of such written notice of the decision of the city in accordance with state law.
(f) Determination that animal is a dangerous or potentially dangerous dog. If the city decides the animal should not be destroyed, the city shall determine whether such animal shall be classified as a dangerous dog or potentially dangerous dog. If the city determines that such dog shall be classified as a dangerous dog or potentially dangerous dog, the owner shall promptly be given written notice thereof, and the dog shall continue to be impounded by city until the owner shall have complied with all the requirements of this article, after which the animal will be returned to the owner. If the owner fails to meet said requirements within ten business days following written notice of the decision of the authorized official classifying of the dog as a dangerous dog or potentially dangerous dog, or to timely request a hearing appealing such decision, the dog shall be humanely destroyed in accordance with state law; provided, however, that the city may extend said time for up to an additional 15-day period upon payment by the owner of the per diem boarding costs for said dog.
(g) Fees and costs. The owner of an animal confiscated under the provisions of this section shall pay a fee of $50.00 and reimburse the city for all costs of housing, feeding, and any medical treatment of said animal.
(Code 1989, § 9-3-7; Ord. of 9-8-2008, § II(9-2-4(C))
259:
It shall be unlawful to keep more than two dogs or two cats on any one lot; provided, however, that an exception is made and an additional dog may be kept on a lot when the occupant or owner of the premises has a medical need or is handicapped and the dog in question is a trained animal used to benefit or aid a handicapped or medically ill individual.
(Ord. of 9-8-2008, § II(9-2-4(J)(1))
260:
(a) It shall be unlawful for any owner or custodian of any cat to allow the cat to roam free on the property of another without permission of the owner or person in possession of that property, or without such cat wearing a collar with a current rabies tag attached.
(b) It shall be unlawful for any owner or custodian of any dog to allow the dog to roam or run free on the property of another without the permission of the owner or person in possession of that property, or without such dog wearing a collar with a current rabies control tag attached.
(Ord. of 9-8-2008, § II(9-2-4(J)(6), (7))
261:
Every female dog or cat, which is not sterilized, during the period it is in heat shall be confined in a building or other enclosure in such a manner that such female dog or cat cannot come into contact with another animal of the same species or breed, except for planned breeding.
(Ord. of 9-8-2008, § II(9-2-4(D)(4))
State Law reference— Permitting dogs in heat to run free prohibited, O.C.G.A. § 4-8-6.
262: The owner, keeper, walker or person in charge of any dog shall not permit solid fecal matter of such animal to deposit on any street, alley, or other public or private property, unless such matter is immediately removed therefrom by said owner or person in charge. This section shall not apply to a person who is visually or physically handicapped.
263:
It is unlawful for the owner or custodian of a dog or cat to allow such animal to run at large in the city.
(Ord. of 3-11-2002, § 9-3-12(a))
264:
It shall be a violation of the article for the owner of any dog or cat to allow the dog or cat to act so as to become a public nuisance dog or cat as defined in this chapter. The owner of any dog or cat which has been classified as a nuisance dog or cat by the animal control unit shall have a right to appeal such classification, in writing, to the city court. The decision of the city court shall be final.
(Ord. of 3-11-2002, §§ 9-3-12(b), 9-3-20)
265:
It shall be a violation of this article for the owner to permit a dog or cat off the premises of that owner's property without a collar and identification tag for each animal. The identification tag shall give the name, current address, and telephone number of the owner.
(Ord. of 3-11-2002, § 9-3-12(c))
268:
Any person owning, keeping, harboring, or having custody of any dog or cat over four months of age within this municipality must obtain a license as herein provided.
(Ord. of 3-11-2002, § 9-3-35(a))
269:
(a) Application for a license must be made within 30 days after obtaining a dog or cat over four months of age; provided, however, that this requirement will not apply to a nonresident keeping a dog or cat within the municipality for no longer than 60 days. Each license shall be renewed between January 1 and January 31 of the year following issuance and each year thereafter.
(b) Written application for licenses, which shall include the name and address of the applicant and a description of the animal, shall be made to the licensing authority, accompanied by a license fee in the amount provided in the city fee schedule and a rabies certificate issued by a licensed veterinarian or anti-rabies clinic.
(Ord. of 3-11-2002, § 9-3-35(b), (d), (e), (k), (n))
270:
The licensing period shall begin with the fiscal year and shall run for one year. A license application may be made 30 days prior to, and up to 60 days after, the start of the fiscal year. Persons applying for a license during the licensing year shall be required to pay one-half of the fee stipulated in this section.
(Ord. of 3-11-2002, § 9-3-35(c), (i))
271:
Fees for original issuance of licenses and renewal and duplicates thereof shall be in the amounts provided in the city fee schedule. License fees shall not be required for certified service dogs, governmental police dogs, or other certified dogs that are trained to assist the physically handicapped.
(Ord. of 3-11-2002, § 9-3-35(e))
272:
Upon acceptance of the license application and fee, the licensing authority shall issue a durable tag or identification collar, stamped with an identifying number and the year of issuance. Tags should be designed so that they may be conveniently fastened or riveted to the animal's collar or harness. Dogs and cats must wear identification tags or collars at all times when off the premises of the owners.
(Ord. of 3-11-2002, § 9-3-35(f), (g))
273:
The licensing authority shall maintain a record of the identifying numbers of all tags issued and shall make this record available to the public at all times.
(Ord. of 3-11-2002, § 9-3-35(h))
274:
No person may use any license for any animal other than the animal for which it was issued.
(Ord. of 3-11-2002, § 9-3-35(m))
275:
A duplicate license may be obtained upon payment of a replacement fee in the amount specified in the city fee schedule.
(Ord. of 3-11-2002, § 9-3-35(l))

279:
(a) Required; issuance. It is unlawful for an owner to have or possess within the city limits a dangerous or potentially dangerous dog without a certificate of registration issued in accordance with the provisions of this division. At the time of the renewal of a certificate of registration, an animal enforcement agent or police officer shall require evidence from the owner or make such investigations as may be necessary to verify that all requirements of this division continue to be met. Issuance of a certificate of registration or the renewal of a certificate of registration by the city does not warrant or guarantee that the requirements specified in subsections (b) and (c) of this section were met or are maintained by the owner of a dangerous or potentially dangerous dog.

280:
The owner or custodian of a dangerous or potentially dangerous dog shall post a clearly visible sign on the premises where the dog is located warning that there is a dangerous dog on the property. Such sign shall prominently display the dangerous dog symbol designed by the state department of natural resources pursuant to O.C.G.A. § 4-8-25(b)(2)(B).
(Ord. of 3-11-2002, § 9-3-29(b))
281:
The owner or custodian of a dangerous or potentially dangerous dog shall acquire and maintain at all times in full force and effect a policy of insurance in the amount of at least $15,000.00 issued by an insurer authorized to transact business in this state insuring the owner of the dangerous dog against liability for any personal injuries inflicted by the dangerous dog. Alternatively, the owner or custodian shall acquire and maintain a security bond in the amount of $15,000.00 or more issued by a surety company authorized to transact business in this state payable to any person or persons injured by the dangerous dog.
(Ord. of 3-11-2002, § 9-3-29(c))
282:
The owner of a dangerous or potentially dangerous dog shall notify the city animal control office immediately if the dog is on the loose, is unconfined, has attacked a human, has died or has been sold, donated, or disposed of. If the dog has been sold, donated, or disposed of, the former owner shall provide the animal control office with the name, address, and telephone number of the new owner of the dog. The owner of the dangerous or potentially dangerous dog shall notify the city animal control office if the owner is moving from the incorporated portion of the city.
(Ord. of 3-11-2002, § 9-3-29(d), (e))
283:
It is unlawful for an owner of a dangerous or potentially dangerous dog to permit the dog to be outside a proper enclosure unless the dog is muzzled and restrained by a substantial chain or leash and is under the physical restraint of a responsible person. The muzzle shall be made in a manner that will not cause injury to the dog or interfere with its vision or respiration but will prevent it from biting any person.
(Ord. of 3-11-2002, § 9-3-30)
286:
Upon receiving a report of a dangerous dog or potentially dangerous dog within an animal enforcement agent's jurisdiction from a law enforcement agency, animal control agency, rabies control officer, or county board of health, the animal enforcement agent shall make such investigations and inquiries with regard to such report as may be necessary to carry out the provisions of this article.
(Ord. of 3-11-2002, § 9-3-27; Ord. of 9-8-2008, § II(9-2-4(I)(1))
287:
As applied to the owners of potentially dangerous dogs, the procedures provided in this division must be carried out as a necessary condition for the enforcement of the provisions of this division against such owners. As applied to the owners of dangerous dogs, the procedures provided in this division shall not be an essential element of any crime provided for in this article.
(Ord. of 3-11-2002, § 9-3-28(a); Ord. of 9-8-2008, § II(9-2-4(I)(2))
289:
(a) The city shall conduct hearings when requested under this section by the owner aggrieved by a decision of an authorized officer with respect to classifying such owner's dog as a dangerous dog or a potentially dangerous dog, or the reclassification of a potentially dangerous dog as a dangerous dog.
(b) Request for hearing shall be made by the animal owner within five business days of receiving a notice of a right to request such hearing. Any person who requests a hearing, provided for in this section but who, after receipt of notice of the hearing, fails to appear at said hearing shall be deemed to have abandoned the hearing request and the decision of the authorized officer which was to be the subject of such hearing shall be affirmed and final.
(c) The owner of an animal requesting a hearing shall pay the additional daily boarding and other fees as established in this article. Failure to pay the fees and costs assessed against the owner, if affirmed by the city, shall constitute an abandonment of any claim to the animal and will result in the animal being disposed of as otherwise provided in this article.
(Ord. of 3-11-2002, § 9-3-28(d); Ord. of 9-8-2008, § II(9-2-4(I)(2)(c), (M)(1))
290:
At the hearing, the owner of the dog shall be given the opportunity to testify and present evidence and, in addition thereto, the court shall receive such other evidence and hear such other testimony as the court may find reasonably necessary to make a determination either to sustain, modify, or overrule the enforcing officer's classification of the dog.
(Ord. of 3-11-2002, § 9-3-28(d); Ord. of 9-8-2008, § II(9-2-4(I)(2)(c))
291:
Within ten days after the date of the hearing, the court shall notify the dog owner in writing by certified mail of its determination on the matter. If such determination is that the dog is a dangerous or potentially dangerous dog, the notice shall specify the date upon which the determination is effective, provided that the effective date shall be not less than ten days after the date of this order.
(Ord. of 3-11-2002, § 9-3-28(e); Ord. of 9-8-2008, § II(9-2-4(I)(2)(d))
294:
The animal enforcement agent or police officer is authorized to make whatever inquiry is deemed necessary to ensure compliance with the provisions of this article. Law enforcement agencies of the city shall cooperate with the animal enforcement agent in enforcing the provisions of this article.
(Ord. of 3-11-2002, § 9-3-29(g))
295:
(a) Dangerous dogs. A dangerous dog shall be immediately confiscated by the animal enforcement agent or police officer or by any law enforcement officer or by any other person authorized by the animal enforcement agent or chief of police if the owner or custodian of the dog does not secure and maintain the required liability insurance or bond, the dog is not registered as required in this article, or the dog is not maintained in a proper enclosure or properly restrained outside a proper enclosure.
(b) Potentially dangerous dogs. A potentially dangerous dog shall be confiscated in the same manner as a dangerous dog if the dog is not registered as required in this article or the dog is not maintained in a proper enclosure or properly restrained outside a proper enclosure.
(Ord. of 3-11-2002, § 9-3-31(b), (c))
296:
(a) Any dog that has been confiscated under this article shall be returned to its owner upon the owner's compliance with the provisions of this article and upon the payment of reasonable confiscation costs including a daily boarding fee, a pickup fee, and a rabies vaccination fee if the animal's owner does not produce proof of a current rabies vaccination. The amount of all fees shall be as set forth in the city fee schedule.
(b) In the event the owner or custodian of a dangerous dog or potentially dangerous dog has not complied with the provisions of this article within 20 days of the date the dog's classification as a dangerous dog or potentially dangerous dog, as the case may be, becomes final or, in the case of a dog previously so classified, 20 days of the date the dog was confiscated, the dog shall be destroyed in an expeditious and humane manner in accordance with state law; provided, however, upon a showing of good cause, the city may extend said time, for up to an additional 15-day period, upon the payment by the owner of the per diem boarding costs for said dog.
(Ord. of 3-11-2002, § 9-3-31(c); Ord. of 9-8-2008, § II(9-2-4(I)(4)(a))
297:
(a) Fine and imprisonment. In addition to any other penalties imposed by state law, the owner of a dangerous dog or potentially dangerous dog who violates the provisions of this article or whose dangerous dog or potentially dangerous dog is subject to confiscation under this article shall be subject to penalties as provided in section 1-14.

(Code 1989, § 6-2-9)
302:
The city has created and established the office of building inspector. The building inspector is appointed by the mayor and city council and serves at their pleasure. The building inspector is charged with the duty of enforcement of this chapter and shall perform other duties as may be prescribed by the mayor and city council. The building inspector appointed by the city council may be a city employee or a county employee.
(Code 1989, § 6-2-2)
305:
(a) It is unlawful for any person to set up any mobile home within the city or to erect, construct, enlarge, alter, repair, move, remove, convert, or destroy any building or structure within the city if the cost of construction will exceed $1,000.00 without first having obtained a building permit. Application for a building permit shall be made to the building inspector on forms prescribed by the city council and shall be accompanied by a fee in the amount provided in the city fee schedule and such additional information and supporting documentation as the building inspector may require.

(c) Issuance of a permit upon plans and specifications shall not prevent the building inspector or city from thereafter requiring the correction of errors in such plans and specifications, or from thereafter preventing building operations being carried on thereunder when in violation of chapter 40, pertaining to zoning, or of any other chapter of the city. Permits for construction and uses which require a conditional use or variance to the general requirements of chapter 40, pertaining to zoning, shall be issued by the building inspector only upon order of the city council.
(Code 1989, §§ 6-2-1, 6-2-3; Ord. of 1-12-2009, § 9.02)
306:
No permit shall be issued for the construction, alteration, remodeling, or placement of any building, sign, structure, or manufactured home, until a written application is filed with the city by the owner of the property affected or by the authorized agent of such owner. The application shall at a minimum:
(1) Include all forms as may be provided by the zoning administrator or other city representative for such purpose, and must include all required information on the forms by the applicant.
(2) Include a surveyors plat of the property affected.
(3) Include a detailed statement as to the proposed use of the building or land for which a permit is sought.
(4) Include plans in duplicate drawn to scale showing the actual dimensions and shape of the lot to be built upon; the exact sizes and locations on the lot of buildings already existing, if any; the location and dimensions of the proposed building, sign, manufactured home, or alteration.
(5) If the development for which the permit is other than a single-family or small agricultural use, a more formal site plan may be required by the zoning administrator. This site plan shall be provided in triplicate and submitted with the application and shall show the following at a scale not more than 50 feet to the inch:
a. Title, if any, under which the proposed development is to be recorded and the name of the present owner.
b. Names of owners of adjacent property.
c. A topographic map showing the location of existing property lines, streets, alleys, buildings, easements, watercourses, and other physical site features, including the location of existing trees of four inches or larger in caliper as measured at breast height.
d. The exact size, shape, and location of the building or structure to be erected thereon with exact distances from the building or structure to property lines and street rights-of-way.
e. Other proposed improvements, landscaping, or buffers proportionally and exactly dimensioned.
f. Proposed method of water supply, sewage disposal, and storm drainage.
g. All proposed uses of the property to be developed appropriately indicated on the plan.
h. Other information as may be required to insure compliance with the provisions of this chapter.
i. Date, north arrow, and graphic scale.
j. The name and address of a registered surveyor or engineer chosen by the applicant who is authorized to stake the road lines and location of such proposed development.
(6) Other such information as may be required by the zoning administrator to determine compliance with and provide for enforcement of this chapter.
(7) In addition, the zoning administrator may require certified "as-built" site plans or other information necessary to determine chapter and initial permit compliance before issuing a certificate of occupancy.
(Ord. of 1-12-2009, § 9.03)
307:
If the application for a building permit is not approved, the building inspector shall immediately notify the applicant in writing on the application the cause for denial. Upon receipt of notice, the applicant may re-apply for a building permit, provided he overcomes, to the satisfaction of the building inspector, the causes for the previous denial, or he may institute appeal proceedings.
(Code 1989, § 6-2-4)
308:
If, in the opinion of the building inspector, the valuation of the building, alteration, or structure appears to be underestimated on the application, the application for building permit shall be denied, unless the applicant can show detailed estimated costs to meet the approval of the building inspector. Permit valuations shall include total costs, such as plumbing, electrical, mechanical equipment and other systems.
(Code 1989, § 6-2-5)
309:
Any person failing to obtain a building permit before commencing construction shall be punished by fine of not more than $100.00 or imprisonment for a term not exceeding 30 days or both of these punishments.
(Code 1989, § 6-2-6)
313: The city's technical codes are remedial in nature, and shall be construed to secure the beneficial interests and purposes thereof, which are public safety, health, and general welfare through structural strength, stability, sanitation, adequate light and ventilation, and safety to life and property from fire and other hazards attributed to the built environment including alteration, repair, removal, demolition, use and occupancy of buildings, structures, or premises, and by regulating the installation and maintenance of all electrical, gas, mechanical and plumbing systems (herein "service systems").
314: Quality control of materials and workmanship is not within the purview of this Code except as it relates to the purposes stated herein.
315: The inspection or permitting of any building, system or plan under the requirements of this Code shall not be construed in any court as a warranty of the physical condition of such building, system or plan or their adequacy. Neither the city nor any employee thereof shall be liable in tort for damages for any defect or hazardous or illegal condition or inadequacy in such building, system or plan, nor for any failure of any component of such, that may occur subsequent to such inspection or permitting.
316: Where in any specific case sections of the technical codes, of this Code, and of state or federal laws or regulations specify different materials, methods of construction or other requirements, the most restrictive shall govern. Where there is a conflict between a general requirement and a specific requirement, the specific requirement shall be applicable.
317: Appendices referenced in the code text of the technical codes shall be considered an integral part of the codes.
318: Standards referenced in the text of the technical codes shall be considered an integral part of the codes. If specific portions of a standard are denoted by code text, only those portions of the standard shall be enforced. Where code provisions conflict with a standard, the code provisions shall be enforced. Permissive and advisory provisions in a standard shall not be construed as mandatory.
319: Any requirements necessary for the strength, stability or proper operation of an existing or proposed building, structure, electrical, gas, mechanical or plumbing system, or for the public safety, health and general welfare, not specifically covered by this or the other technical codes, shall be determined by the building inspector.
320: The provisions of the technical codes are not intended to prevent the use of any material or method of construction not specifically prescribed by them, provided any such alternate has been reviewed by the building inspector. The building inspector shall approve any such alternate, provided the building inspector finds that the alternate for the purpose intended is at least the equivalent of that prescribed in the technical codes, in quality, strength, effectiveness, fire resistance, durability and safety. The building inspector shall require that sufficient evidence or proof be submitted to substantiate any claim made regarding the alternate.
321: Alterations, repairs or rehabilitation work may be made to any existing structure, building, electrical, gas, mechanical or plumbing system without requiring the building, structure, plumbing, electrical, mechanical or gas system to comply with all the requirements of the technical codes, provided that the alteration, repair or rehabilitation work conforms to the requirements of the technical codes for new construction. The building inspector shall determine the extent to which the existing system shall be made to conform to the requirements of the technical codes for new construction.
322: If the occupancy classification of any existing building or structure is changed, the building, electrical, gas, mechanical and plumbing systems shall be made to conform to the intent of the technical codes as required by the building inspector.
326:
A public officer or five residents of the city may file a request with the building inspector, or the building inspector may make such a motion on his own, charging that a structure is unfit. The building inspector will make a preliminary investigation to determine if there is a basis for the charges. If he finds there is a basis, he will issue and cause to be served a complaint upon the owner of and any parties in interest in such structure. The complaint will state the charges and contain a notice that a hearing will be held before the building inspector or his designated agent at a place within the city not less than ten days nor more than 30 days after the serving of the complaint.
(Code 1989, § 6-5-2)
327:
The owner and any parties in interest have the right to file an answer to the complaint and appear in person, or otherwise, and give testimony at the hearing. The rules of evidence prevailing in courts of law or equity shall not be controlling in the hearings before the building inspector.
(Code 1989, § 6-5-3)
328:
(a) After notice and hearing, the building inspector may determine that a dwelling is unfit for human habitation of its current commercial or business use if he finds conditions in the structure that are dangerous or injurious to the health, safety or welfare of the occupants of the dwelling or of neighboring dwellings or of other residents in the municipality. Such conditions may include but are not limited to, dilapidation, disrepair, structural defects, uncleanliness, lack of adequate ventilation, lack of adequate light, lack of adequate sanitary facilities, and defects increasing the hazards of fire, accidents, or other calamities. The building inspector shall state in writing his findings of fact in support of his determination.
(b) If the building inspector finds the structure is not unfit, the matter will be closed. If the building inspector finds the structure is unfit, his findings of fact must include a determination of whether the cost of repair would exceed one-half the value such structure will have when repaired to satisfy the minimum requirements of law.
(Code 1989, § 6-5-4)
329:
The building inspector shall issue and cause to be served upon each person in possession of the property, each owner, and each party in interest an order:
(1) If the repair, alteration or improvement of the structure can be made at a reasonable cost in relation to the value of the structure, requiring the owner or parties in interest within a time specified in the order to repair, alter, or improve the structure so as to render it fit for human habitation or its current commercial use or to vacate and close the dwelling as a human habitation; or
(2) If the repair, alteration or improvement cannot be made at a reasonable cost in relation to the value of the structure, requiring the owner to remove or demolish the structure.
In no event shall the building inspector order removal or demolition except upon a finding that the cost of repair exceeds one-half the value such structure will have when repaired to satisfy the minimum requirements of law.
(Code 1989, § 6-5-5)
330:
(a) Complaints or orders issued by the building inspector shall in all cases be served upon each person in possession, each owner and party in interest. The return of service signed by the building inspector or his agent or an affidavit of service executed by any state citizen shall be sufficient evidence of service.
(b) Service upon parties who reside outside the municipality shall be by the sheriff or any other duly authorized law enforcement or other officer of the county of the residence of such party or by any duly authorized citizen. The return of such sheriff or deputy of the affidavit of such citizen stating that the parties were served either personally or by leaving a copy of the complaint or orders at their residence shall be conclusive as to service.
(c) Nonresidents of this state shall be served by publishing the notice once each week for two successive weeks in the local newspaper. A copy of the complaint or orders shall be posted in a conspicuous place on the premises affected. If the address of the nonresidents is known, a copy of such complaint or orders shall be mailed to them by registered or certified mail.
(d) If the whereabouts of any owner or party in interest is unknown and cannot be ascertained in the exercise of reasonable diligence, the building inspector shall make an affidavit to that effect and service shall be made by publication as provided in this section for nonresidents. In the alternative, service may be made upon any person, firm or corporation holding itself out as an agent for the property involved.
(e) A copy of such complaint or orders shall also be filed in the proper office or offices for the filing of lis pendens notice in the county in which the structure is located. Any such complaint or orders or an appropriate lis pendens notice may contain a statement to the effect that a lien may arise against the described property and that an itemized statement of such lien is maintained on a lien docket maintained by the city clerk.
(Code 1989, § 6-5-6)
331:
(a) If the owner or parties in interest fail to comply with an order to vacate and close or demolish the structure, the building inspector may cause such structure to be repaired, altered or improved or to be vacated and closed or demolished. He may cause to be posted on the main entrance of the structure so closed a placard with the following words:
"This building is unfit for human habitation or commercial, industrial, or business use; the use or occupation of this building for human habitation or for commercial, industrial, or business use is prohibited and unlawful."
(b) Before the building inspector may exercise the duties outlined in this section, an ordinance must be passed by the mayor and council finding that the specific structure is unfit and ordering the building inspector to proceed to effectuate the purpose of this article.
(Code 1989, § 6-5-7)
332:
(a) The cost of vacating and closing or removal or demolition by the city shall be a lien against the real property upon which such costs were incurred. The lien shall attach upon the payment of all costs of demolition and the filing of an itemized statement of the total sum of the costs by the building inspector in the office of the city clerk on a lien docket maintained by the clerk for such purposes.
(b) If the structure is removed or demolished by the building inspector, he shall sell the material from the structure and credit the proceeds of the sale against the cost of the removal or demolition. Any balance remaining shall be deposited in the superior court by the building inspector, shall be secured in such manner as may be directed by the court and shall be disbursed by the court to persons found to be entitled thereto by final order or decree of the court.
(Code 1989, § 6-5-8)
333:
The city may enforce the collection of any amount due on such a lien for demolition or removal of a structure in the following manner:
(1) The owner or parties at interest shall be allowed to satisfy the amount due by paying to the city within 30 days after the perfection of the lien, a sum of money equal to 25 percent of the total due. The remaining balance together with an interest rate of seven percent per annum shall be paid to the city in three equal annual payments, each of which will come due and payable on the anniversary date of the initial payment.
(2) Should the property upon which the lien is perfected be sold, transferred, or conveyed by the owner or parties at interest at any time prior to the termination of the three-year period, then the entire balance shall be due and payable to the city.
(3) Should the amount due on such lien, or any portion thereof, be unpaid after the passage of the three-year period or upon the occurrence of the contingency provided for in subsection (2) of this section, the city may enforce collection of any amount due on such lien for alteration, repair, removal, or demolition of such structure. Collection will be made pursuant to state law.
(Code 1989, § 6-5-9)
334:
All the provisions of this article, including method and procedure, may also be applied to private property where an accumulation of weeds, trash, junk, filth and other unsanitary or unsafe conditions shall create a public health hazard or a general nuisance to those persons residing in the vicinity. A finding of any governmental health department, health official or building inspector that such property is a health hazard shall constitute prima facie evidence that the property is in violation of this article.
(Code 1989, § 6-5-10)
337:
The purpose of this article is to establish that all lots, houses, buildings, offices, and structures within the corporate limits of the city shall be properly and orderly numbered in accordance with the master plan of proper and orderly numbering as established by the mayor and council.
(Code 1989, § 6-10-1)
338:
The city shall keep a chart showing proper street numbers and shall assign to every building or lot the proper number by which it is to be designated.
(Code 1989, § 6-10-2)
339:
It shall be the duty of the owners and occupants of every house or building within the city limits to have placed thereon, in a place visible from the street, figures at least 2½ inches high, showing the proper number of such house or building.
(Code 1989, § 6-10-3)

342:
The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this chapter, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning:
Administrative fee means the component of the occupation tax which approximates the reasonable cost or handling and processing the occupation tax.
Administrator means the city clerk who may be assisted by employees of the clerk's office.
Employee means an individual whose work is performed under the direction and supervision of the employer and whose employer withholds social security contributions, federal income tax, or state income tax from the individual's compensation or whose employer issues to such individual for purposes of documenting compensation a form W-2, but not a form 1099.
Location or office means any structure or vehicle where a business, profession, or occupation is conducted, but shall not include a temporary or construction work site which serves a single customer or project, or a vehicle used for sales or delivery by a business or practitioner of a profession.
Occupation tax means a tax levied for revenue purposes on persons, partnerships, corporations or other entities for engaging in an occupation, profession or business in the city.
Occupation tax certificate means a document issued by the city acknowledging payment of the occupation tax and administrative fee.
Practitioners of professions and occupations means those individuals listed in O.C.G.A. § 48-13-9(c)(1)—(18) but does not include a practitioner who is an employee of a business if such business pays an occupation tax.
Regulatory fee means a fee that approximates the cost of regulatory activity by the city.
Regulatory fee certificate means a document issued by the city acknowledging payment of a regulatory fee.
(Ord. of 12-12-1994, § 1(7-1-1); Ord. of 12-11-1995, § 7-1-1(D))
343: This chapter is applicable not only to those business entities specifically mentioned herein, but also to businesses that may be the topic of other chapters of this Code to the extent this chapter includes regulations not included in those chapters.
